correctness.rationale: The theorem is reconstructed from the exact orthogonal Gaussian decomposition Av=(a+Delta W)v+Delta sqrt(W(1-W))u with W~Beta(q/2,p/2), and the independent Student ratio U=Z/chi_k. Below/above interval events yield the two regularized beta functions. Gamma ratios give each boundary contribution and the min(p,q)/2 scale. An explicit positive-part beta integral yields mean overshoot and conditional mean, with controlled endpoint domination by bounded small-u integrals and arbitrarily high inverse-chi moments for large k. The regularly varying density of U and beta integration produce the fixed-k tail constant; the strict moment threshold follows by tail integration. The standalone checker validates symbolic identities, finite-row special cases, exact beta quadrature, tail constants, and 960000 independent Gaussian sketches, but finite checks are not treated as infinite proofs. Not proved: multilevel spectra, non-Gaussian sketches, finite precision.

value.rationale: Spectral-envelope inclusion is a natural invariance of symmetric Rayleigh–Ritz; a non-symmetric sketched inner product may fail it. The finding measures both occurrence and size, quantifies distinct rates controlled by the smaller extreme eigenspace multiplicity, and separates frequency \(k^{-r/2}\) from mean severity \(k^{-r/2-1}\) and rare \(t^{-k}\) tails. These exact positive constants supply a meaningful stress-test benchmark for randomized eigenvalue methods, especially at very small sketch sizes; the theorem does not extrapolate to every eigensolver or guarantee better performance.
